thread:
maria_ss: FYI — AcmeHealth (Enterprise) just escalated. They say theres a public disclosure for a crypto key-wrapping bug that maps to our KMS handler (customer-facing private deployments + Redwood Private). They want: ETA for patch, mitigation steps they can show auditors, and a clear log/audit snapshot proving no exfiltration. Also noted increased 500s and latency spikes starting ~06:00 UTC. Can we triage?

ashwin_sec: Triage started. Im looking at the CVE details and matching function signatures in our KMS shim. Filing a ticket in tracker: RDW-SEC-2026-241. Short answers first: - Hotfix candidate exists (needs build + canary). - Immediate mitigation: disable remote wrapping, force local-only key ops, rotate affected wrapping keys. - ETA for customer-facing patch note: initial mitigation guidance in 4h, binary hotfix + canary in 24-36h, full rollout 48-72h depending on canary results.

maria_ss: Copy. Customer asked for an official statement they can present to their security team and auditor (POC that were treating this as high severity). They also want sample audit logs showing KMS RPCs over the last 30 days. Is that possible?

ashwin_sec: Yes — we can pull audit logs (storage + syslog) but must redact secrets. Two things: 1) we can provide a sanitized recent audit snapshot showing KMS:Encrypt/Decrypt/WrapKey calls by principal id and IP, with timestamps. 2) For on-prem/private installs, we can provide a checklist for customers to demonstrate no external key material was exported. Ill coordinate with SRE for log export.

ops-bot: Alert created: INC-2026-8113. Assigned: andre_sre, samir_rt. Priority: P0. Link: https://internal.redwood/incident/INC-2026-8113

andre_sre: Picking this up. Im already seeing the latency/500 pattern on the KMS path (service:kms-wrapping). Spike graph: `sum(rate(kms_wrap_errors[1m]))` shows a jump at 2026-03-15T06:09Z. Early hypothesis: retry storms from upstream clients hitting fallback logic when wrapping fails.

jess_cs: Adding customer repro notes from AcmeHealth support thread: they called `POST /v1/kms/wrap` with optional param `mode=remote` and got 502s + connection resets. Example HTTP snippet they sent:
```
POST /v1/kms/wrap HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.example
Authorization: Bearer xxxxx
Content-Type: application/json
{ "key_id": "acme-prod-wrap-1", "data": "<base64>...", "mode": "remote" }
```
Response: 502 + `backend: key-wrap-failed` in body.

samir_rt: Repro confirmed in staging with `mode=remote`. Root cause: deserialization mismatch on the new key-wrapping protobuf if the client sends a deprecated envelope flag. Patch is a 6-line fix in `kms/handler.go` plus a small schema bump. I can produce a patch and build a canary image tonight. Steps I recommend for customers immediately: 1) set `mode=local` for KMS ops if their deployment allows it (forces local HSM ops, bypassing vulnerable path), 2) rotate wrapping keys with `rotate-key --force`, 3) if on Redwood Private, disable remote key import until patch applied.

maria_ss: Customer also asked about HSM/KMS hardware: does this affect HSMs (YubiHSM/CloudHSM) or only our software wrapper? They need to know whether keys in HSMs could be exposed.

ashwin_sec: Short answer: vulnerability affects our software key-wrapping path (the code that orchestrates HSM operations), not the HSM firmware itself. If the customer uses a certified HSM and were only orchestrating via standard PKCS#11 calls, the hardware cryptography remains intact. However, because the orchestration can mis-handle a wrapping envelope, an attacker with access to that orchestration path could potentially cause mis-wrapping. So we must treat wrapped key metadata as potentially impacted and rotate. I'll draft a security bulletin for the customer that explains this and lists mitigation steps for auditors.

andre_sre: For audit logs: I can export a salted/redacted bundle of `kms.audit.*` events covering the customer tenant for the last 30 days — includes caller, operation, key_id, ip, and unique request id. We will mark any entries that look anomalous for follow-up. Note: log export will take ~2 hours to fully sanitize for external sharing.

jess_cs: AcmeHealth legal wants a timeline they can show auditors within the next 8 hours. Can we promise a mitigation guide + sanitized audit snapshot in that window?

ashwin_sec: We can promise a mitigation guide + high-level sanitized audit example in 8 hours. Full sanitized 30-day bundle is 2-3 hours after that (so within ~10-12 hours). Hotfix binary will take longer (24-36h). We should be explicit in the customer statement about timelines.

samir_rt: Ill start the hotfix PR now: `git checkout -b fix/kms-wrap-proto` -> small code change -> CI build + e2e. Canary plan: route 1% of KMS traffic from Hosted API to the canary image, monitor `wrap_success_rate` + `latency_p50/p95`. If green for 3 hours, increment to 10%, then 50%. Rollback criteria: >0.5% increase in wrap errors or p95 > 250ms.

maria_ss: Good. Customer also had a related billing question: they saw doubled request counts because their client retried on 502s. They want to pause billing or get a credit while we investigate. Support, can we tag these requests and reverse billing?

jess_cs: We can create a billing adjustment ticket referencing INC-2026-8113 and the request IDs from their account. If we get the request-id list from audit export, finance can process a partial credit. Ill start the billing ticket and request the request-ids export from SRE.

andre_sre: FYI logs snippet of the error (redacted):
```
[2026-03-15T06:10:12Z] request_id=abc123 tenant=acme op=WrapKey key=acme-prod-wrap-1 err=deser:envelope_v2:unexpected_field
[2026-03-15T06:10:12Z] request_id=abc124 tenant=acme op=WrapKey err=io:connection-reset
```
This matches the deserialization mismatch Samir mentioned.

ashwin_sec: I'll draft the customer-facing security advisory now. Points to cover: scope (which deployments are affected), immediate mitigations (mode=local, rotate keys, disable import), expected timelines (mitigation doc in 4h, audit snapshot in 8-12h, hotfix rollout 24-72h), and our offer for an executive call. Ill post the advisory here for review before we send it.

maria_ss: Thanks — please @channel when advisory is ready. Also include a short Q&A for auditors (did keys leave HSM? was key material exported?) so customers can attach to their evidence packs.

ops-bot: Updated INC-2026-8113: status=investigating -> mitigation_in_progress. Linked PR: https://internal.redwood/repo/pulls/1429.

samir_rt: PR opened and CI passing on linux/amd64: https://internal.redwood/repo/pull/1429. Can build canary image now. Ill schedule the 1% canary for 2026-03-15T22:00Z (UTC) pending final security signoff.

maria_ss: Great. Lets keep comms tight — Ill coordinate the customer call in 1 hour and will use the draft advisory.

ashwin_sec: Draft posted: https://internal.redwood/sec/notice/2026-03-kms-wrap. Please review ASAP (esp. legal and support).

jess_cs: Reviewed and gave small wording edits. Preparing the customer note + legal cover.

andre_sre: Continuing log forensics and will flag anomalous principals. If anything suspicious shows key export attempts, we escalate to incident response.

maria_ss: Thanks team. Ill update the customer after the advisory review.

[end of thread]
